To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

electrogenerated tags can be used for on‐line counting of sulfhydryl residues in peptides during mass spectrometry, and that this approach can be used to improve the confidence in protein identification.

the electrochemically induced tagging of peptides containing cysteine residues by substituted hydroquinone compounds provides a powerful method for the identification of cysteine peptides and for the discrimination of protein candidates in a peptide mixture.

the electrotagging method is a powerful post‐column treatment to enhance the peptide identification score and to discriminate against other protein candidates in the case of gel‐free peptide mapping strategies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the on‐line determination of the number of cysteine amino acids in peptides by electrogenerated tags.
the development of new strategies for the on‐line cysteine content determination of peptides during ESI‐MS analysis.
a new strategy to improve peptide identification in proteomic studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cysteine‐tagging method can be applied to any peptide sample and is a powerful technique to improve protein identification.
the electrochemically induced tagging of cysteine in peptides is a powerful tool for protein identification in a gel‐free approach.
the electrotagging method is a useful tool for the analysis of cysteine‐containing peptides and proteins, and it can provide additional information in the protein identification process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the on‐line cysteine quantitation by electrogenerated tags is a promising tool for protein identification and characterization.
electrochemical tagging of cysteine is a useful method for cysteine content determination in peptides and proteins, and it is compatible with the on‐line peptide mapping strategy.
this electrochemical tagging method is a promising tool for peptide mapping and proteome analysis, especially for proteins with low molecular weight and high content in cysteine residues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electrochemical tagging of cysteine in peptides during ESI‐MS can provide a powerful tool for protein identification and quantification.
the electrochemical tagging of peptides containing cysteine residues can be used for the identification of proteins, especially in the case of low‐abundance proteins.
the electrochemical tagging method can be used as a complementary strategy to enhance the protein identification score in the case of low‐resolution MS instruments.
